items.title: [Palimpsest analysis] China censorship today: network layer elevated in the latest board synthesis
items.summary: Palimpsest cross-instrument analysis. 8 of 10 selected censorship instruments are current. The evidence spans attention, silence, network interference, erasure, and app distribution, but their denominators remain separate.
items.content_text:
ITEM TYPE: PALIMPSEST CROSS-INSTRUMENT ANALYSIS

China's information controls must be read as separate content, network, erasure, and distribution measurements rather than one seductive national score.

The board detects movement, not motive

Upstream board reports: single layer elevated: network. 39 of 39 configured sources report; 32 are live. Health qualifiers: 3 degraded, 4 stale. The board-wide e-value is 4.534; the predeclared board alarm threshold is 20. The board statistic tests whether named signals moved beyond their own histories; it does not identify one cause for the movement. The current coverage audit marks 0 signal as confounded by its measurement coverage.

Attention, silence, and erasure answer different questions

The current deletion-directive index ranks 211 terms with documented censorship provenance. No current finding is published for Silence index because the source status is degraded. No current finding is published for Erasure observatory because the source status is stale. The directive index counts provenance-bound terms, the silence index tests a predeclared blackout rule, and the erasure index summarizes heterogeneous layers; placing them together does not create one censorship rate.

Network measurements agree on scope, not on one denominator

The current coverage-weighted fusion of reporting vantages is 28.8%. The current OONI aggregate reports a 58.6% anomaly index across 273,143 completed China measurements. The current controlled panel reports 100% blocked responses across 5 tested domains. The fused index, volunteer-probe aggregate, and fixed inside-China panel use different samples and protocols, so none can be substituted for a national share of traffic or users.

App availability needs both a fixed panel and a broad corpus

The current panel finds 60% of 10 tracked apps unavailable in the China storefront. The current AppleCensorship corpus reports 28.13% unavailable among 110,255 tested apps for mainland China. The fixed panel supports controlled same-round comparison, while the broad corpus improves catalogue coverage; neither percentage identifies why an individual app is absent.

What today's reading can support

At the edition clock, 8 of 10 selected instruments publish current claims and 2 publish availability warnings instead. The defensible conclusion is a layered description of current observations, not a single estimate of censorship prevalence or intent.
